newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN OPPOSITION STEPS UP PROTESTS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN OPPOSITION STEPS UP PROTESTS.

text.p: Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) is stepping up anti-government protests to call for early parliamentary elections, UDF leader Ivan Kostov said on Tuesday.
"The BSP has proved that it has no potential to lead the country out of the crisis so we will take our responsibility to head the people's protest," Kostov told a news conference.
The UDF has scheduled street rallies in Sofia on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.
Tens of thousands of protesters marched in Sofia last week and in two major cities on Monday to protest against shrinking wages eroded by the collapsing national currency.
On Tuesday, rallies to call for early elections were scheduled in the Black Sea ports of Varna and Bourgas, in Vidin and in Stara Zagora.

The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) on Tuesday nominated Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev as prime minister to replace Zhan Videnov, who resigned on December 21 after criticism of his management of the economy during his two years in office.
"We still hope that some of the Socialist deputies are concerned about the interests of Bulgaria rather than those of the party and will support the UDF salvation declaration," Kostov said.

On Friday, parliament began debating the "salvation declaration" presented by the opposition last month, calling for elections to be held in March, and negotiations with the IMF and World Bank on an economic programme to be conducted by an all-party team.

The UDF says a fixed exchange rate regime under discussion with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will fail under the present government and it wants a new central bank board appointed to implement the currency board mechanism.
Voting on the declaration is expected on January 10.
Kostov said that the UDF will discuss more protest actions if parliament rejects the declaration.
